NONE: › a film, poem, or book that is long and contains a lot of action, usually dealing with a historical subject
（通常指描寫歷史題材的）長篇敍事式電影（或書籍）；史詩
› in the style of an epic
史詩般的；鴻篇巨製的；壯麗的
› used to describe events that happen over a long period and involve a lot of action and difficulty
艱苦卓絕的；漫長而艱難的
› informal extremely large
宏大的；極大規模的
› informal extremely good
極好的

example: It's one of those old Hollywood epics with a cast of thousands.
這是老牌的好萊塢史詩電影之一，演員陣容達到數千人。
an epic film about the Roman Empire
古羅馬帝國題材的史詩電影
an epic journey/struggle
漫長艱難的旅途／艱苦卓絕的鬥爭
The problem of inflation has reached epic proportions.
通貨膨脹問題已經到了極其嚴重的地步。
The Hulk roller coaster ride was epic.
坐綠巨人雲霄飛車實在是太棒了。

NONE: › belonging to both sexes, or characteristic of the opposite sex
兼具男女兩性特徵的

example: She noted his epicene features - the long eyelashes, the full lips.
她注意到他的女性特徵——長長的睫毛和飽滿的嘴唇。

NONE: › the point on the earth's surface directly above an earthquake or atomic explosion
（地震）震央；（原子彈爆炸的）中心，爆炸點
› a part that sticks out at the end of a bone, often where muscles and tendons are attached
上髁（骨上的隆起）

example: Inflammation of the epicondyle of the radius caused by overuse of the forearm is sometimes called tennis elbow.
因為前臂的過度使用而引起的橈骨上髁發炎有時被稱為網球肘。

NONE: › a person who enjoys high quality food and drink
講究飲食的人；美食家

example: Synonym
gourmet

NONE: › getting pleasure from food and drink of high quality
好美食的；講究飲食的
› an
epicure

C: › [ C ] the appearance of a particular disease in a large number of people at the same time

C usually singular: › [ C usually singular ] a particular problem that seriously affects many people at the same time

NONE: › happening a lot and affecting many people
流行的；盛行的；肆虐的

example: a flu epidemic
流感的傳播
a crime/unemployment epidemic
犯罪頻發／大範圍失業
Crime and poverty are epidemic in the city.
犯罪和貧窮如瘟疫一般在這個城市肆虐。

NONE: › relating to epidemiology
流行病學的

example: an epidemiological study/survey
流行病學研究/調查

NONE: › the scientific study of diseases and how they are found, spread, and controlled in groups of people
流行病學
› the thin outer layer of the skin
表皮
› a tube that carries sperm from the testes (= the two round male sex organs)
附睾，副睾

example: Harmless cysts may occur in the epididymis.
附睾中可能生長良性胞囊。

NONE: › an anaesthetic (= a substance that stops you feeling pain) that is put into the nerves in a person's lower back with a special needle
硬膜外麻醉

example: They gave my wife an epidural when she was giving birth.
我妻子分娩時，醫生給她施行了硬膜外麻醉。

NONE: › relating to the central upper part of the abdomen (= the lower part of the body, containing the stomach, bowels, and other organs)
上腹部的
› a small flat part at the back of the tongue that closes when you swallow to prevent food from entering the tube that goes to the lungs
（舌頭後部的）會厭
› a short saying or poem that expresses an idea in a clever, funny way
詼諧短詩；警句；雋語

example: One of Oscar Wilde's most frequently quoted epigrams is "I can resist everything except temptation".
奧斯卡•王爾德最常被引用的雋語之一就是「我可以抗拒一切，誘惑除外」。

NONE: › a saying or a part of a poem, play, or book put at the beginning of a piece of writing to give the reader some idea of what the piece is about
（詩歌、戲劇或書的卷首或章節前的）引言，卷首語
› an electric device that removes hairs from your face or body by pulling them out
電動除毛器
› a condition of the brain that causes a person to become unconscious for short periods or to move in a violent and uncontrolled way
癲癇，羊癇瘋，羊角風

example: She can't drive because she suffers from/has epilepsy.
她不能開車，因爲她患有癲癇。

NONE: › suffering from or caused by epilepsy
患癲癇的；由癲癇引起的
› someone who has epilepsy
癲癇患者

example: an epileptic fit
癲癇發作
Her aunt is epileptic.
她姑姑患有癲癇。

NONE: › a speech or piece of text that is added to the end of a play or book, often giving a short statement about what happens to the characters after the play or book finishes
（戲劇的）收場白，收場戲；（書的）結尾部分，後記，跋

example: Compare
prologue

NONE: › a hormone that is made naturally in the body and may be given as a drug
腎上腺素

example: Epinephrine is used medicinally to treat asthma.
腎上腺素被用來治療哮喘。
Synonym
adrenalin

NONE: › a moment when you suddenly feel that you understand, or suddenly become conscious of, something that is very important to you
（對重要事物的）頓悟
› a powerful religious experience
（對宗教真諦的）頓悟
› a Christian holy day in January (traditionally 6 January in Western Christianity) that celebrates the revelation of the baby Jesus to the world
顯現節，主顯節（1月6日，紀念賢士朝拜耶穌的日子）
› relating to the epiphysis (= the rounded end of a long bone where it joins another bone)
骨端的，骨骺的

example: Epiphyseal fractures are serious because bone marrow is lost through the fracture site.
骺骨折是非常嚴重的，因為骨髓會在折斷處流失。

NONE: › the rounded end of a long bone where it joins another bone
骨端，骨骺（長骨關節端的擴大部分）
› a plant that grows on another plant but does not feed from it, for example, some mosses
附生植物，著生植物（生長在另一植物上卻從別處獲得養料的植物，如苔蘚）
› a thin sheet of tissue that develops across the centre of the retina (= the area at the back of the eye that receives light)
視網膜前膜，黃斑前膜（症）

example: An epiretinal membrane does not cause blindness but does affect central vision.
視網膜前膜並不會造成失明，但是會影響中心視力。

NONE: › of or relating to a bishop or a Church that is directed by bishops
主教的；主教管轄的
› a member of the Episcopal Church
蘇格蘭聖公會教徒；美國聖公會教徒
› belonging or relating to the Episcopal Church
聖公會教徒的

C: B2 a single event or group of related events
事件；（相關的）一連串事件；一段經歷
B2 one of the single parts into which a story is divided, especially when it is broadcast on the television or radio
（尤指電視或廣播節目的）一集，一節，片斷

example: This latest episode in the fraud scandal has shocked a lot of people.
詐騙醜聞最新爆出的事件讓很多人瞠目結舌。
The drugs, the divorce, and the depression - it's an episode in his life that he wants to forget.
吸毒、離婚和抑鬱——這是他人生中不堪回首的一段經歷。

NONE: › happening only sometimes and not regularly
偶爾發生的；不定期的
› Episodic stories are divided into several parts, especially when they are broadcast on the television or radio.
（尤指電視或廣播節目）有許多片段的

example: The war between these two countries has been long-drawn-out and episodic.
這兩個國家之間時斷時續的戰爭持續了好多年。
an episodic drama series
一部（分集的）連續劇

NONE: › relating to knowledge or the study of knowledge
知識的；認知的
› the part of philosophy that is about the study of how we know things
認識論
› formal a letter
書信
› one of the letters written to the early Christians by the apostles (= the first men who believed in Jesus Christ)
使徒書信

example: humorous Many thanks for your lengthy epistle, which arrived in this morning's post.
今晨收到你寫來的長信，非常感謝。

NONE: › a short piece of writing or a poem about a dead person, especially one written on their gravestone
悼文；悼亡詩；（尤指）墓誌銘
› relating to the epithelium (= the layer of cells that cover most surfaces of the body)
上皮的，上皮組職的

example: Epithelial cells form tissues that make up organs such as skin and glands.
上皮細胞形成組織，組織構成器官，比如皮膚和腺體。

NONE: › a layer of cells covering all the surfaces of the body except the interior of blood and lymph vessels
上皮，上皮組職
› an adjective added to a person's name or a phrase used instead of it, usually to criticize or praise them
（通常指在褒貶人時使用的）表述形容詞，修飾語

example: The singer's 104-kilo frame earned him the epithet of "Man Mountain" in the press.
這位歌劇演員身材魁梧，體重104公斤，在新聞報道中他因此而被冠以「巨人」的稱號。

NONE: › the typical or highest example of a stated quality, as shown by a particular person or thing
典型；典範

example: Even now in her sixties, she is the epitome of French elegance.
即使現在已經年屆花甲，她仍堪稱法國人優雅風度的典範。

NONE: › to be a perfect example of a quality or type of thing
是…的典型；成爲…的典範

example: With little equipment and unsuitable footwear, she epitomizes the inexperienced and unprepared mountain walker.
她幾乎沒有帶任何裝備，穿的鞋也不合適，是一個典型的缺乏經驗、準備不足的登山客。
